text.p: Italian bond futures opened on a lower track but soon pushed firmer helped by further denials of a conflict of interest by prime minister Romano Prodi related to his judicial problems, dealers said.
"After further denials by Prodi reported in Italian newspapers this morning, the market would seem a buy and after a nervous start that seems to be the case, said one LIFFE trader.

Futures saw a sell-off late Tuesday on bund and T-bond weakness, but also due to comments by PDS leader Massimo D'Alema that if Prodi fell there would have to be new elections. The PDS is the largest party in the centre-left government coalition.

On Monday, a deputy public prosecutor in Rome asked for Prodi to be tried for alleged abuse of office and conflict of interest relating to the time of his chairmanship of state company IRI. Prosecutors alleged irregularities concerning the sale by IRI in October 1993 of food company Cirio.
Dealers said with T-bonds ending mixed overnight and little international news to influence BTPs, the focus this morning was largely on domestic issues.
"There was no reason for panic on the D'Alema comments and some operators just thought it was time to take some profits," said the LIFFE trader.
Dealers pointed out that most politicians have supported Prodi who has continually denied any wrongdoing and calls for him to step down have been few.
